requirement_text: Proof of sufficient knowledge of the German language is required to enroll. This proof should be provided through the results of the German Language Proficiency Test for Admission to Higher Education (DSH). A DSH 2 certificate is sufficient to start in all degree programs that are taught in German (with the exception of Master of Education degree programs requiring DSH 3). Alternative Proof for DSH 2 Examination: TestDaF Level 4 in all 4 sub-modules; the aptitude test from a German preparatory college (FSP); the German Language Diploma (level II) from the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs of the Länder of the Federal Republic of Germany (DSD II); Goethe-Certificate C2; telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule; Austrian Language Diploma C2 (ÖSD C2).

requirement_text: Applicants for the Bachelor's programs in Molecular Biomedicine, Media Studies, Musicology/Sound Studies, Geography, Archaeologies, Economics and Computer Science, Economics Major and Economics Minor at the University of Bonn who do not have a German Abitur are required to provide proof of English language proficiency. In addition to the required German language skills (DSH 2 or equivalent), applicants with foreign certificates must have English language skills at the B2 level (CEFR). The appropriate English certificate must be submitted by the application deadline. An exemption from the English language certificate is possible in the following cases: The language of instruction at secondary school or in a completed bachelor's degree program was English. Official confirmation from the school/university is required. The English exam subject is marked with B2 in the secondary school leaving certificate. Recognized English language certificates and their minimum requirements: TOEFL: Internet-based test (iBT): with a minimum score of 72. Test Date Score applies, not MyBest Score. Please note: TOEFL ITP is not accepted. Please tell ETS the code number D393 so that your TOEFL score report will be sent directly to the University of Bonn. IELTS Academic with a minimum score of 5.5 (Overall band score). Cambridge English: B2 First. TELC ENGLISH Certificate B2. PEARSONS PTE Academic 59. UNICERT II Vantage. [Molecular Biomedicine is named in the affected-programme list.]
source_authority_note: uni-bonn.de fails looksOfficial() (no .edu/.ac./.gov suffix) — this is the institution's own official page. Needs the officialDomains-provenance fix documented in source-authority-gap.md, not a lowered evidence bar.
limitations: Named exclusions apply within the TOEFL option: 'Test Date Score applies, not MyBest Score' (MyBest Score composite not accepted) and 'TOEFL ITP is not accepted' (a different, non-iBT TOEFL product is categorically rejected). A numeric TOEFL match alone does not satisfy this requirement if the score derives from either excluded source.
researcher_notes: Applies only to applicants who do not hold a German Abitur (i.e. is keyed to qualification type, not citizenship — an EU or non-EU applicant with a German Abitur is exempt; a German citizen without one is not). TOEFL '72' is unambiguously the pre-2026-rescale 0–120 total scale (72 makes no sense on the new 1–6 scale); the page carries no cutover-date qualifier and states a TOTAL score only (no per-section breakdown), so it is satisfiable via ETS's 0–120 comparable score (available on score reports through January 2028) and does not exhibit the Glasgow-style partially-unsatisfiable subtest defect.

requirement_text: Local numerus clausus (DoSV): Applicants begin by registering on the hochschulstart.de website before submitting their actual application via the University of Bonn's application system. requirement_text: Study places in degree programs subject to an institution-specific local admission restriction (local numerus clausus) are allocated applying the following quotas: 20% of study places are allocated based on the university entrance qualification, i.e. best Abitur grades (Abiturbestenquote). 80% of study places are allocated applying the University Admissions Selection Procedure (Auswahlverfahren der Hochschulen, AdH). Under the AdH, 20% of study places are only allocated according to the result of the university entrance qualification (AdH Leistung). The remaining 60% are allocated based on university entrance qualification grade applying a maximum seven semesters of waiting time (AdH Leistung und Wartezeit). Rankings are calculated with a maximum 100 possible ranking points, converting Abitur grade and semesters of waiting time to point values on published conversion tables.

researcher_notes: Grade/point conversion table (1.0 Abitur = 70 points down to 4.0 = 0 points) and waiting-time conversion table (7 semesters = 30 points down to 0 = 0 points) both published on-page; condensed here rather than reproduced in full. Same explicit domestic (EU/EEA + equivalent) scope as the DoSV record.

requirement_text: An adequate knowledge of English at level B2 CEFR, proven in one of the following ways: IELTS test score (preferably 6.0 or higher), TOEFL test score (preferably 87 or higher), Cambridge English First (FCE). Applicants who have received a degree from a study program taught entirely in English can ask their university to certify that English was the only medium of instruction in their program. ... proof of English proficiency at level B2 CEFR by means of either: a TOEFL test score (preferably of 87 or higher) ... an IELTS test score (preferably of 6.0 or higher); other internationally recognized language certificates, e.g. the Cambridge English First (FCE); a document issued by your home university certifying that English was the medium of instruction; an Abiturzeugnis if it proves an English language proficiency at B2 level CEFR. German proficiency: Not required.

researcher_notes: Distinct from and additional to the university-wide Bachelor's-level English-B2 requirement recorded separately for 8 named Bachelor's programmes — this is this specific Master's programme's own policy. IMPORTANT SHAPE DIFFERENCE: the numeric test scores here ('preferably 87 or higher', 'preferably 6.0 or higher') are explicitly advisory/preferred, not stated as hard minimums — the actual binding requirement is 'B2 CEFR', evidenced through any of several routes including non-numeric ones (home-university English-medium-of-instruction letter, Abiturzeugnis). A scalar threshold check against '87' alone would misrepresent this requirement as a hard numeric gate when the source explicitly frames it as a preference within a broader, multi-path B2 proof requirement. TOEFL 87 is unambiguously the legacy 0–120 total scale (no cutover date stated, total score only, no subtest breakdown) — satisfiable via ETS's comparable score through January 2028.
